question: Which platform has the best soft skills training for employees, like communication and emotional intelligence?
text:
If you’re choosing a platform specifically for employee soft skills—communication, emotional intelligence, conflict management, teamwork, leadership—I’d put LinkedIn Learning first overall, with Coursera for Business a close second.

My ranking
Platform	Best for	Soft-skills quality	Employee/L&D fit
LinkedIn Learning	Broad workplace soft skills	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Coursera for Business	Deeper, structured learning	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐½
Udemy Business	Huge variety & practical courses	⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐
Specialist providers	High-impact EQ/leadership programs	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	⭐⭐⭐⭐
🥇 Best overall: LinkedIn Learning

LinkedIn Learning for Business

I'd choose this if your goal is getting a large number of employees to actually use the training.

It has dedicated learning paths covering emotional intelligence, communication, teamwork, resilience, critical thinking and management. For example, its current Professional Soft Skills Learning Pathway has 12 courses/10 hours, including emotional intelligence and communication. 
L
LinkedIn
+1

It also has a Human Skills for Managers certificate covering emotional intelligence, effective communication, motivating employees and leading through change. 
L
LinkedIn

Why I'd pick it: short, workplace-oriented courses + easy employee adoption + very broad catalog.

🥈 Best for deeper learning: Coursera for Business

Coursera for Business

Coursera is stronger if you want more substantial learning experiences rather than mostly short professional-development videos.

For example, its current offerings include courses on workplace emotional intelligence, practical communication, active listening, empathy and conflict management. 
C
Coursera
+1
 It also offers structured specializations around business communication, including stakeholder communication, negotiation, empathy and emotional intelligence. 
C
Coursera

Why I'd pick it: better when you want employees to develop a skill systematically and demonstrate completion/learning.

🥉 Best for variety: Udemy Business

Udemy Business

Udemy's advantage is the enormous range of individual courses and instructors. You can find very specific training—for example, communication + EQ + difficult conversations + leadership—rather than having to fit employees into a predefined curriculum. 
U
udemy.com

The trade-off is that the quality and teaching style can vary more, so I'd curate the courses rather than simply giving employees the entire catalog.

Want measurable, structured skill development: Coursera for Business

Want maximum course variety and flexibility: Udemy Business

Managers specifically: LinkedIn Learning is particularly compelling because of its dedicated human-skills/manager paths. 
L

Communication + emotional intelligence as the core objective: I'd shortlist LinkedIn Learning and Coursera first.

One important caveat: if you're looking for behavior change rather than simply "courses employees can take," I'd look beyond the big content libraries to specialist providers that use practice, role-play, coaching, simulations and manager reinforcement. That's often much more effective for skills like empathy, difficult conversations and emotional regulation.

If you tell me roughly how many employees you have, your budget per employee, and whether you're primarily training individual contributors or managers, I can narrow this down to the 3 best platforms and compare their pricing, content, AI features, analytics, and ROI.
